text:
amy: Quick sync — we need to decide on a canonical policy for trailing-slash and prefix normalization in the gateway. Noticed inconsistent behavior between host-anchored routes and prefix routes in staging.

amy: Example of current fuzziness:
```
- route A: host: api.example.com, path: /v1/foo
- route B: host: api.example.com, path: /v1/foo/
- route C: prefix: /v1/foo
Requests to /v1/foo and /v1/foo/ sometimes hit different targets.
```

amy: Questions: default normalize to drop trailing slash? redirect 301/307? keep strict matching? and how does this interact with prefix vs exact path precedence? :thinking_face:

devon: +1 on a single canonical form. My vote: normalize server-side to a canonical path (no trailing slash) for routing decisions, but offer an opt-in redirect flag per route for web clients. That keeps internal consistency and lets web teams opt into SEO-friendly redirects.

devon: Suggested precedence pseudocode:
```
1) exact path match (literal, after normalization)
2) longest literal host+path
3) longest normalized prefix route
4) wildcard/regex fallback
```
This handles /v1/foo vs /v1/foo/bar and avoids surprising prefix grabs.

raj: I worry about changing semantics for existing customers. Some apps treat slash as meaningful (file vs folder). We should preserve exact-match semantics if a route explicitly includes trailing slash (i.e., if user configured path with trailing slash, treat it as exact unless they opt into normalization). For prefix routes, normalizing makes more sense.

raj: Proposal: two-layer policy:
- "exact" routes: match exactly as configured (no normalization)
- "path/prefix" routes: by default normalize trailing slash for matching, but expose a flag `preserve_trailing_slash=true` to opt out.

infra-bot: route-compiler v2.14 deployed to staging: compiled 1,234 routes. Note: automatic normalization applied to 91 prefix routes ("/v1/foo/" -> "/v1/foo"). See logs: /deploys/1912345678/logs

lina: UX note: console should show the canonical form and the raw configured form side-by-side (Configuration | Canonical URL). Also add a small badge when a route's behavior is changed by normalization so SREs can audit rollouts.

amy: Good points. If we do mixed behavior (exact keep, prefix normalize), we need clear precedence rules and a short migration path doc and deprecation warnings. Also we should add an API validation warning when a new route would shadow an existing one due to normalization.

devon: Implementation detail: route matcher should compare using normalized tokens and keep an additional "configured_path" field to show original. That lets compiler detect collisions and emit warnings.

raj: For redirects, keep it out of default — opt-in only. Redirects add latency and change client semantics.

amy: Action items:
- devon: write RFC for normalization rules & precedence (include pseudocode and perf impact) — due EOW
- eng-qa: add tests for trailing slash permutations (exact vs prefix) across host permutations
- console: lina to mock small UI change for canonical vs configured path badge
- infra: add compiler warning when normalization causes shadowing (infra-bot: please add a log event type)

amy: Anyone object to that plan? :thumbsup: or say now.

devon: :thumbsup:
raj: :thumbsup:
infra-bot: ack — will emit event `normalization.shadow_warning`

lina: will share mock by tomorrow.

amy: Thanks — I'll start the RFC draft and tag y'all.
